Subject: MAP: Prefetch + batching assumptions — econ audit & close timeline

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our agreement on the mutual action plan, I pulled together a concise econ audit focused on two levers you flagged: prefetch/prefix caching and batching behavior for short-chat flows. Attached is a single-sheet MAP with key milestones and an assumptions tab (REDWOOD_MAP_prefetch-econ.xlsx). High-level summary below so your procurement and SRE teams can review quickly.

Why this matters: for HealthGrid’s triage assistant we expect a large fraction of prompts to share stable prefixes (patient intake/context). Proper prefetching + prefix KV caching can reduce token generation count by ~18–40% depending on how often the cache hits and whether we can serve from a quantized variant for non-sensitive queries. Batching reduces per-token overhead but increases tail latency — we modeled both 90th/95th percentile tradeoffs.

Key assumptions in the sheet (short):
- Baseline prompt size: 180 tokens; average response: 120 tokens.
- Prefetch effectiveness: low/med/high scenarios (10% / 25% / 40% token reduction).
- Batch window: 0ms (no batching), 12ms, 40ms (simulated).
- Serving variants: fp16 (baseline) and int8-ptq (lower cost, ~20% throughput uplift on our dedicated pool).
- SLO target: 95th percentile generation < 220 ms for patient-facing flows (we mark acceptable configs).

Eval plan (MAP milestone 2):
- 2-week A/B using a 10k queries/day sampling window from a subset of customers (can run inside your staging VPC).
- Measure tokens/user, cache hit-rate, 95p latency, and per-req cost.
- Success criteria: tokens/$ improvement >= 15% and 95p latency within SLO (or documented trade-off accepted).

Next steps I propose this week:
1) You to confirm whether prefetching can be applied to the first-turn prompts we discussed (Naveen looped).
2) Your SRE to share target 95p latency requirement and any hard upper bounds for batching-induced latency.
3) We finalize the MAP spreadsheet and schedule a tech walkthrough (30m) with Ben.

If it helps, I can run a short sensitivity run on your sample logs this afternoon to populate the mid-case numbers.

Thanks,
Aisha

Thanks Aisha — this is helpful and very clear. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we spin up an eval: 

1) Prefetching: Yes, we can mark the first-turn intake templates as eligible for prefetch/prefix caching — most patient flows use the same 5–6 tokens at the start.
2) Latency SLOs: For patient-facing chat we want 95p <= 250ms, hard ceiling 350ms.
3) Sampling: We can expose a 5k queries/day steady stream from staging for the A/B initially (we prefer a slower ramp).

One ask: can you surface the per-token cost change in the spreadsheet per scenario (we need that for procurement)? If we get a >20% tokens/$ improvement in the mid-case we can move Contract Review faster.

Samir / Aisha —

Quick technical notes and what we'll include in the eval harness (Ben, SE):

- Prefetch/prefix cache model: We'll implement a per-customer in-memory prefix KV cache in the Canary environment. For evaluation we assume TTL=24h and eviction LRU — the sheet models hit-rates at 10/25/40% across conversation distributions.
- Batching model: Redwood supports dynamic batching with a max window; in the spreadsheet I used 12ms and 40ms to show conservative/optimistic batch capture. Real capture depends on concurrency and arrival patterns — we'll instrument at 1ms granularity for the first week.
- Cost model detail: tokens/$ column uses our hosted pricing equivalent and then applies a delta when serving from int8 variant (cost multiplier 0.78) and when prefix cache reduces generation tokens. We'll also include per-request orchestration overhead (0.5—0.9 cents) to be conservative.
- Edge case: For any requests touching PHI, we will not serve from shared quantized variants unless HealthGrid confirms acceptability; the MAP has a flag for "sensitive" routes.

I'll prepare an additional tab with a short Monte Carlo sensitivity (1000 draws) to show median and 90p tokens/$ uplift; will attach by EOD.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachment(s): latency-profiles.csv (sample traces), REDWOOD_MAP_prefetch-econ.xlsx (updated with technical notes)
